chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

When Yusuf (peace be upon him) met his brother, he said: 'O my brother! How were you able to marry women after me?' He replied: 'My father commanded me.' He said: 'If you are able to have offspring who will fill the earth with glorification (of Allah), then do so.'

key_terms.التَّسْبِيح: Glorification of Allah — the act of saying 'SubhanAllah' (Glory be to God), a cornerstone of Islamic worship
key_terms.تُثْقِلُ الْأَرْض: To make the earth heavy — an idiomatic expression meaning to fill the earth abundantly with a quality
key_terms.ذُرِّيَّة: Offspring, progeny — in Islamic usage, righteous descendants who carry on worship and divine remembrance

ai.seo_question: Why did Prophet Yusuf's brother marry despite the family's difficult circumstances?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) narrates a conversation between the Prophet Yusuf (Joseph) and his brother after their reunion in Egypt. Yusuf, who had suffered years of separation and imprisonment, asks his brother how he could bring himself to marry during such times of family tragedy. The brother explains that their father — the Prophet Ya'qub (Jacob) — had commanded him to marry, motivating him with the noble purpose of producing righteous offspring who would glorify God and fill the earth with tasbih (divine praise). This hadith places marriage within the grand prophetic tradition of perpetuating a community devoted to God's glorification, grounding marriage in spiritual rather than merely worldly objectives.
